family.tagline: Gardens by day, violin in the evening, quotes on the Core.
family.story: Kwame designs and builds gardens, and his crew starts at seven. Imogen teaches violin in the lounge in the evenings. The jobs, the quotes and the lesson calendar all live in one house.

companion.name: Efua
companion.job: Drafts quotes and client emails from the site notes Kwame texts it.
companion.limits: Drafts only. Kwame reads and sends every quote.

companion.name: Corin
companion.job: Opens AudioMass in its own browser and trims the practice recording Imogen names.
companion.limits: Trims a copy. Imogen keeps the original.

popup.title: A parcel for the farthest room
popup.body: The Den is the farthest room from the front door. Kwame carries the parcel there anyway, past the stair hall, the dining room and the kitchen.

popup.title: What is in the parcel
popup.body: Imogen unpacks four things: the Companion Core, a power cable, a quick-start guide and a recovery USB drive. The Core's footprint is about three quarters of a sheet of paper.

popup.title: Plug it in
popup.body: Kwame plugs the cable in beside his laptop and presses the button. The Core wakes and opens its own Wi-Fi network.

popup.title: Join it from a phone
popup.body: Imogen joins the Core's own network from her phone. Then she chooses the home network and types its password.

popup.title: Pick your first agents and apps
popup.body: In Companion Hub, Kwame picks Hermes and Imogen picks OpenClaw. They add Twenty, Planka and Navidrome. Then they walk away.

beats.capability: talks to you through the messaging platform you pick

popup.title: Efua says good morning
popup.body: Kwame texts the agent he named Efua. She answers before the coffee cools, and the Core is running.
popup.note: Messages pass through the chat service you choose.

say.speaker: kwame
say.text: Morning, Kwame. I am Efua. What is first?

beats.capability: a real-time Kanban board for a team or a family project

popup.title: The week's jobs, with coffee
popup.body: Before seven, Kwame sets the week's jobs on a Planka board. The crew reads it at the kitchen island, coffee in hand.

beats.capability: track the pantry, shopping lists, recipes, chores and household habits in one place

popup.title: A rainy day, a hungry crew
popup.body: Rain stops the work, so the crew stays for lunch. Imogen checks the pantry list in Grocy and adds what the cupboards lack.

beats.capability: control and automate your smart home from one place, locally

popup.title: Lights on before the crew
popup.body: At six-thirty the garage lights come on from a Home Assistant schedule. The Core runs the schedule and reaches the lights over the home Wi-Fi.

beats.capability: track time per project and client, with reports

popup.title: Hours by job, not by guess
popup.body: As the trucks leave, Kwame starts a Kimai timer for each job. At the end of the week the report shows the hours per job.

beats.capability: browse and share your photo library, with automatic tagging, without uploading it anywhere

popup.title: Site photos, filed on the Core
popup.body: At day's end the crew's site photos go into PhotoPrism over the home Wi-Fi. It tags them automatically, and Kwame finds a job by its pictures.

beats.capability: keep customers, deals and custom fields in a CRM you host yourself

popup.title: A new client, filed before lunch
popup.body: A client calls about a hedge and a patio. Kwame adds the address and the site notes to Twenty, the CRM on the Core, before he forgets.

beats.capability: talks to you through the messaging platform you pick

popup.title: Efua drafts the quote
popup.body: Kwame texts Efua the site measurements. Efua drafts the quote. Kwame checks every line and sends it himself.

say.speaker: kwame
say.text: Here is the draft quote. Please check each line.

beats.capability: send invoices and quotes, track expenses and time

popup.title: The quote becomes an invoice
popup.body: When the patio is finished, Kwame turns the accepted quote into an invoice in Invoice Ninja. He tracks the expenses beside it.

beats.capability: store every password in a vault you host; works with the Bitwarden apps

popup.title: Sign-ins stay on the Core
popup.body: Supplier and client sign-ins live in a VaultWarden vault on the Core. Kwame reaches it from his phone with the Bitwarden apps, over the home Wi-Fi.

beats.capability: a small CalDAV and CardDAV server for your calendars and contacts

popup.title: Lesson calendar, kept at home
popup.body: Imogen keeps her lesson calendar and her students' contacts in Baikal. Her phone and her laptop read the same calendar from the Core.

beats.capability: a PDF toolkit that runs in your browser; nothing is uploaded

popup.title: Two pieces, one handout
popup.body: Imogen merges two scores into one handout with BentoPDF. It runs in her browser, and nothing is uploaded.

beats.capability: write notes and a daily journal in plain Markdown files

popup.title: Lesson notes in plain files
popup.body: Imogen writes each student's lesson notes in Logseq, as plain Markdown files on the Core. Next week's page opens beside the last one.

beats.capability: edit audio in a browser tab: cut, fade, normalise, export

popup.title: Corin trims the practice run
popup.body: Imogen names her latest practice recording. Corin opens AudioMass in its own browser and trims the silence from a copy. Imogen keeps the original.

say.speaker: imogen
say.text: The copy is trimmed. The original is where you left it.

beats.capability: stream your own music collection to any device

popup.title: After lessons, her own music
popup.body: When the last student leaves, Imogen plays her own music from Navidrome. The lounge goes back to being a lounge.

beats.capability: track your plants, watering and care history across rooms and beds, with photos and a garden journal

popup.title: The one job he never quoted
popup.body: Kwame logs his own garden in HortusFox. It is the one job he has never quoted.

beats.capability: listen to your audiobooks and podcasts, and pick up where you left off on any device

popup.title: A book that keeps his place
popup.body: While the sprinkler runs, Kwame listens to a book about hedges in Audiobookshelf. It keeps his place when he goes back inside.

beats.capability: draw logos, diagrams and line art as vector graphics, in your browser

popup.title: A planting plan, drawn outside
popup.body: On the deck, Kwame draws a client's planting plan as vector line art in Inkscape. The drawing goes into the quote.

popup.title: Two businesses, one Core
popup.body: Quotes, photos, lessons and a garden journal. The Whitlock-Mensah household runs them all from one Companion Core in the Den.

closing.body: Your jobs, quotes and site photos can run from one Companion Core in the room where you already work. Start the morning with the board.

notes: Owner sign-off open: the FTUE hotspot flow is written as the owner specified and is not on the fact sheet (STORY-BIBLE section 15, item 1).
Chapters follow one working day (kitchen at six forty-five, garage, Den, lounge, garden) instead of the usual living-room-first order. The validator accepts it; showrunner may reorder.
No Companion Memory in this family (cast memory false), so there is no Memory mention.
Den beats anchor on core: the Den has no desk item, the Core sits on the Den desk surface. Fallback is room office.
The seasonal crew (two workers in the cast) appear only as 'the crew', not as members. Payroll is a catalog gap, so Kimai shows hours per job only.
Town Kestrel Hollow and street Alder Furrow Way are invented; still needs the human map check.
